title: Visualization of Germinosomes and the Inner Membrane in Bacillus subtilis Spores
protocol: Streak a bacterial culture on an LB agar plate.
Incubate the LB agar plate overnight at 37°C.
Inoculate a single colony into 5 mL of LB medium in the morning.
Incubate the LB culture under continuous agitation at 200 rpm/min and 37°C until OD600 reaches 0.3-0.4.
Make 500 mL of MOPS medium containing specified nutrients.
Prepare serial dilutions (10^-1 to 10^-7) of the LB culture in MOPS medium.
Incubate the cultures overnight under continuous agitation at 200 rpm/min and 37°C.
Select one of the MOPS dilutions with an OD600 of 0.3-0.4.
Inoculate 0.2 mL of the culture into pre-warmed (37 °C) 20 mL of MOPS medium in a conical 250 mL flask and incubate under continuous agitation until the OD600 reaches 0.3-0.4 (~7 h).
Inoculate the MOPS based sporulation medium (250 mL) with 1% (v/v) pre-culture from step 1.3.1 and incubate for 3 days at 37 °C in a conical liter flask under continuous agitation.

Add 2 µg/mL FM4-64 probe to the sporulation medium 1 or 2 h after reaching the peak OD600 value of vegetative growth (generally approximately 2) and allow the culture to subsequently sporulate whilst protecting it from light.
Determine the sporulation yield using phase contrast microscopy at 100X magnification to distinguish the phase bright spores from phase dark cells.
Pellet the spores at 4,270 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Wash the spore pellet 2-3 times with 40 mL of sterile ultra-pure Type 1 demineralized water.
Spin down the spore pellet at each wash at 4,270 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Suspend the spore pellet in 750 µL of 20% nonionic density gradient medium.
Load the suspension onto 800 µL of 50% nonionic density gradient medium in sterilized microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge for 60 min at 21,500 x g.
Suspend the spore pellet in 200 µL of 20% nonionic density gradient medium.
Load the suspension onto 1 mL of 50% nonionic density gradient medium in a microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge for 15 min at 21,500 x g.
Wash the spore pellet 2-3 times with 1.5 mL of sterile ultra-pure Type 1 water.
Spin down the spore pellet between each wash at 9,560 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Suspend the final spore preparation in sterile ultra-pure Type 1 water to a final OD600 of approximately 30.
Store aliquots of the spores at -80 °C.
Treat PS4150 spores with 0.1 M NaCl/0.1 M NaOH/1% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS)/0.1 M dithiothreitol (DTT) at 70 °C for 1 h.
Wash the spores 10 times with sterilized ultra-pure Type 1 water.
Pre-clean high precision coverslips with 1 M HCl for 30 min in a gently shaking water bath.
Wash the coverslips twice in ultra-pure Type 1 water.
Store the coverslips in 100% (vol/vol) EtOH.
Let the coverslips dry and verify their clarity before use.
Pre-clean the glass slides in 70% EtOH.
Let the slides dry and verify their clarity before use.
Pre-warm two 70% EtOH cleaned and air dried glass slides for several seconds on a 70 °C heating block.
Drop 65 μL of sterilized 2% agarose held at 70 °C on top of one glass slide.
Place the other glass slide on top to spread the agarose between the slides.
Cut the agarose patch into a 1 x 1cm section after removing one of the glass slides.
Add 0.4 μL of sample (fluorescent microspheres or spores of ~108/mL).
Transfer the patch onto the high precision coverslip by placing the coverslip onto the patch and sliding it off.
Fix a Gene Frame (1.5 x 1.6 cm², 65 µL) onto the dried slide.
Place the coverslip over the frame to seal all corners of the frame.
Capture transmission and fluorescence images of spores on a Structured Illumination Microscope equipped with a 100x oil objective.
Generate images at room temperature without ambient light disturbance.
Clean the 100x objective and the slide with 75% ethanol before imaging.
Focus on 100 nm diameter fluorescent microspheres to optimize point spread function (psf) by adjusting the correction ring until a symmetric psf is obtained.
Select a field of view containing approximately 10 round fluorescent microspheres.
Apply grating focus adjustment for both 561 nm and 488 nm excitation wavelengths as guide for image analysis software.
Focus spores with transmission light and capture a transmission light image in the 16× average mode with 200 ms exposures.
Capture 3D-SIM raw fluorescent images of the spores with the illumination mode “3D-SIM”.
Set camera settings to readout mode Electron Multiplying (EM) Gain 10MHz at 14-bit and EM gain at 175.
Excite the FM4-64 probe in PS4150 spores with 561 nm laser light at 20% power for 400 ms.
Excite GerKB-mCherry in KGB80 spores with 561 nm laser light at 30% power for 1 s.
Excite GerD-GFP in KGB80 spores with 488 nm laser light at 60% power for 3 s.
Set Z-Stack settings to top to bottom mode, 0.2 μm/step, 7 steps for germinosome analysis and 20 steps for IM analysis.
Perform the N-SIM Slice Reconstruction for the FM4-64 stained PS4150 spores’ raw data.
Click the Param button for Reconstruct Slice on the N-SIM pad tab sheet to open the N-SIM Slice Reconstruction window.
Set reconstruction parameters in the N-SIM Slice Reconstruction window.
Click Illumination Modulation Contrast (IMC) and set it to Auto.
Set High Resolution Noise Suppression (HRNS) to 1.00.
Set Out of Focus Blur Suppression (OFBS) to 0.05 as starting points.
Click Reconstruct Slice button in the N-SIM Slice Reconstruction window.
Evaluate quality of reconstructed images using Fast Fourier Transformed (FFT) images and reconstruction score.
Adjust HRNS from 0.10 to 5.00 if necessary.
Adjust OFBS from 0.01 to 0.50 as needed for best parameter settings.
Click Apply button in the N-SIM Slice Reconstruction window after adjustments.
Click Close button to close the N-SIM Slice Reconstruction window.
Make a FM4-64 stained PS4150 spores raw image active.
Click Reconstruct Slice button on the N-SIM Pad tab sheet.
Save the reconstructed image.
Convert 3D-SIM raw images of KGB80 into Pseudo-Widefield images using the SIMcheck utility Raw Data SI to Pseudo-Widefield12 plugin in ImageJ.
Randomly select approximately 25 spores in each inverted transmission image for later germinosome analysis.
Select a total of about 350 (in this example, 346) KGB80 spores across 14 fields of view from two slides.
Count the GerD-GFP and GerKB-mCherry fluorescent foci numbers independently in selected KGB80 spores.
Assess the maximum intensities of each GerD-GFP and GerKB-mCherry focus.
Analyze the integrated intensity of each KGB80 spore’s 3D image using ImageJ, considering the mean integrated intensity value of 7 stacks as the integrated signal intensity.
Determine background intensities by imaging the background strain PS4150 with identical settings.
Regard fluorescent spots in individual KGB80 spores as germinosome foci when they are clearly distinguishable from the background.
Apply one-way ANOVA-tests for significance determination with software Origin 9.0.
Consider P values <0.05 as statistically significant.
Use Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient to evaluate the correlation of GerD-GFP and GerKB-mCherry foci number.
Evaluate the correlation of GerD-GFP and GerKB-mCherry integrated signal intensity measurements.
